initial_failure_explanation: Initial 19 fixture failures: fake next-node cursor lacked request count; repeated fixture reset reused a simulated controller without reset wiring.
Second receipt retains two fixture failures where the test attempted to demote the next native victim without issuing its backup and ACK. The corrected test performs that native sequence.
The final fixture uses fresh actual caches per comparison mode. Production eligibility and ACK-before-release rules were not relaxed to make tests pass.
validated_scope: Thirty-four new frontier cases plus existing Full/Mamba/cache/ACK/receipt regressions: 196 total final cases, not summed with overlapping earlier receipts.
Exact victim prefix order and freed FULL capacity compared with native single-node and chain batching across two deficits and eight priority seeds.
Real CPU allocator/tree and operation merge verify source data survive until simulated ACK and FULL/Mamba Host index mappings remain correct.
Partial Host capacity, enqueue exceptions and ACK failure preserve unsent or unacknowledged source pages; parents of every completed branch remain eligible after a batch boundary.
An eight-node plan probes only the needed head of a 4096-candidate heap; no full-heap copy is made.
limits: CPU-only qualification with simulated DMA. No measured GPU, PCIe, JCT, task quality or causal performance gain.
Batching protects several pending Host destinations simultaneously, which can change Host staging/eviction behavior even when the planned device-victim order is preserved.
Multi-rank GPU correctness and performance remain untested. Existing single-node, chain and unsupported-component fallbacks remain available.
This is a common-path engineering candidate, not a selected paper innovation. Any future comparison must match the common engine optimization in native and the proposed policy.
No V77/V78 application, engine, frozen helper or quality queue was changed. The canonical patch remains selected; this incremental patch has not been registered for GPU.
